<p class="page-deck">A conditional, place-based scenario model for assessing co-benefits and co-costs of climate action across domestic buildings, diet and active travel. The programme separates baseline evidence, scenario action, assignment, physical or behavioural effects, causal pathways, endpoints and valuation, with explicit traceability and locality rules.</p>

**Status:** In Development<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Current Lab Research — Owner-approved current programme of the Cities and Climate Learning Lab.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

## How this project contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Consequences for People and Places](/research/consequences-for-people-and-places.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Where New Evidence Matters](/research/where-new-evidence-matters.html), [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Decision or problem:** How to represent the locally varying benefits, burdens and costs of climate scenarios without obscuring causal, geographic or valuation assumptions.

**Existing evidence:** The model separates baseline evidence, scenario actions, causal pathways, endpoints and valuation so their provenance and applicability can be examined.

**Consequential uncertainty:** Local evidence availability, causal assignment and valuation choices may materially change the consequences represented for a place.

**Consequences examined:** Health, equity and other place-based co-benefits, co-costs and distributional outcomes.

**Evidence status:** Owner-approved programme description; the model is in development.

**Claim boundaries:** Scenarios are conditional appraisals, not predictions or universal transferability claims.

**Next learning question:** Which local evidence and valuation choices most alter scenario conclusions?

### Research facets

**Geographies:** canada, united-kingdom<br>
**Climate domains:** mitigation<br>
**Sectors:** buildings, transport, health<br>
**Methods:** place-based-modelling, economic-appraisal, distributional-analysis

## Research questions

- How can local climate scenarios represent co-benefits and co-costs without obscuring causal assumptions?
- How should evidence, geography and valuation choices be governed and traced?
